description: Saves a flow's steps as the Automations editor's save does: send the COMPLETE new step list in order. Add a step by including it, remove one by leaving it out, reorder by changing the order, and edit one by changing its fields. Every step you keep must be sent in full (start from read('flows'), which returns each step's id, timing, channel, message, who it is for and conditions), because the save replaces the whole list; a step you leave out is removed, and at least one step must remain. Copy each step's id so a reorder keeps that step's own autonomy and copy. A step that reaches the client names channel (sms, email or call) and message_template written with Sergio's merge tags, never a hard-coded business or client name. A step's send mode (draft vs automatic) is not set here; its switch stays the owner's. flow_id and the steps come from read('flows'). Pass the same idempotency_key when retrying.

idempotency_key.description: Your id for this operation (8-128 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -). Reuse it on every retry of the same operation; use a new one for a new operation.

auto_dismiss_on_reply.description: Dismiss this step's task when the client replies.

business_days_only.description: Only counts business days toward the deadline.

channel.description: How the step reaches the client, when it does at all. Omit for a step that contacts nobody.

conditions.description: Plain-language exceptions: a different time or action in some cases. Never repeat the step's own timing here.

deadline_days.description: For a visit-day anchor (booking_day_before_at / booking_day_after_at): whole days before or after the visit.

deadline_minutes.description: A due offset in minutes, when the words are not enough (deadline_anchor says from when).

deadline_time.description: For a visit-day anchor: the business-local HH:MM time of day.

description.description: The step's instructions for whoever does it (internal; never sent to the client).

email_subject.description: An email step's subject line; merge tags allowed.

fallback_message_template.description: Only when the template uses {{Address}}: what a contact with no address on file gets instead.

id.description: The step's stable id, copied from read('flows'). Keep it when reordering or editing so the step keeps its own autonomy and copy pools.

is_read_only_guidance.description: true = guidance the team reads, never a checkable task.

late_policy.description: A booking-anchored step whose due time already passed: send_now (default) or skip.

message_template.description: The exact message a text or email step sends; required for those channels. Message text uses Sergio's merge tags, exactly as spelled: {{Client First Name}} (The recipient's own first name); {{User Company}} (Your business name, exactly as it is set on your organization); {{User First Name}} (The first name of the teammate sending the message (your business profile name when Sergio sends it on its own)); {{Offer}} (This campaign's own offer text, exactly as written on the campaign (e.g. "$29.89 off next booking")); {{Offer Expiry Date}} (The day this client has to book by. The same date every step of their sequence quotes); {{Company Phone Number}} (Your primary business phone number, set once in Settings); {{Business Website}} (Your business website, set once in Settings under Business); {{Review Link}} (Your Google review link, set once in Settings and shared by every message that asks for a review); {{Last Visit Date}} (The date of the client's most recent visit. A contact with no past visit is held for you to write); {{Address}} (The recipient's address on file. For a message about a booking, that booking's address); {{pleasantries}} (A short opener in your voice that fits the day the text actually goes out ("Happy Friday!" on a Friday, "Hope your week is going well!" midweek). Updates on its own if the send time moves. Use it in some messages, not every one); {{Goodwill}} (A closing well-wish in your voice that fits when the text actually goes out ("Have a great weekend!" on a Friday afternoon). Updates on its own if the send time moves). Never hard-code the business name or a client name, and never write a bracketed placeholder like [first name]. {{Offer}} needs offer_text set; {{Offer Expiry Date}} needs offer_expiry_days set. The first text automatically ends with "Reply STOP to opt out.", so do not write it.

only_for.description: The picked Only-for rule (groups and/or contact ids), copied from read('flows'). Absent or empty = everyone.

paused.description: Keep the step in the plan but stop minting it.

scope_phrase.description: The plain-words lead-in for who a step is for, e.g. "For first-time clients".

title.description: What the team does, in a few words (the task's title).

type.description: manual (a person does it; default) or ai_assist (Sergio helps).

when_phrase.description: The owner's words for when the step is due, e.g. "4 hours after we last replied". The compiled timing is derived from it on save, as the editor does it.

within_followup_hours.description: Only send inside the business's follow-up hours.
